correctness.rationale: For n>=4, two unselected A-vertices have identical closed traces exactly when both indices are outside X union Y; the same holds for B. Cross-side equality forces X union Y into at most two indices, impossible when at most one matched index is absent. Coverage holds exactly under the 0/1/>=2 opposite-side selection rules; inclusion-exclusion removes six disjoint classes and yields both polynomials. The minimum-code formulas follow from one selection at each of n-1 distinct indices, with a separate cube boundary proof. Direct adjacency checks of every one of 1,398,016 subsets for n=4..10 match the full bivariate coefficients, and independent symbolic comparisons hold through n=50. The infinite claim rests on the proof, not the finite tests.

originality.rationale: The principal primary paper of Foucaud–Lehtilä (2022) gives universal identifying-code bounds but no crown-specific code polynomial. The 2024 survey explicitly gives the known cube case of 56 minimum codes, which is properly attributed. The closest same-graph 2022 MILD result uses a different witness rule; the crown word-representation paper uses a different invariant. The independently located exact chain-graph and threshold-graph identifying-code theorems cannot specialize to crowns because crowns contain an induced 2K2. An edge-metric-basis crown theorem has a related n-minus-one index-support skeleton but does not supply the all-size, two-part closed-neighborhood identifying-code enumeration. No equivalent all-size bivariate result was found; residual risks are stated.
residual_risks: A prior exact identifying-code enumerator for matching-deleted bicliques, bipartite Kneser H(n,1), or the crown graph may be unindexed or inaccessible.

The edge-metric basis crown theorem overlaps with the minimum-code index-skeleton; minimum-count improvement alone might be viewed as a routine corollary. The novel claim is the full all-size bivariate enumerator.
The n=4 cube count 56 is prior art and is expressly excluded from novelty assertions.

value.rationale: The invariant counts all identifying sensor placements in both bipartition classes independently, providing an exact two-budget distribution for the natural regular family of bipartite Kneser H(n,1) graphs. This directly refines scalar minimum identification parameters, characterizes all nonminimum feasible sets, and identifies the mechanism behind the known cube exception. It is a complete motivated infinite-family enumeration rather than an isolated computation; its value does not depend on claiming the known cube number 56 as new.
